Surgical education

What Should You Know Before Choosing Breast Implants?

Cover implant selection, informed consent, recovery, long-term monitoring and possible revision surgery.

Home/Insights/What Should You Know Before Choosing Breast Implants?

Choosing breast implants is a medical decision as much as an aesthetic one. This guide outlines the areas worth understanding before you commit.

Implant selection

Implant selection depends on individual anatomy, product characteristics, surgical assessment and your preferences. There is no single “best” implant; what suits one person may not suit another.

Informed consent

Informed consent means understanding the procedure, its limitations, its risks and the alternatives — and having the opportunity to ask questions before deciding.

Recovery

Recovery varies according to the technique, individual healing and your surgeon’s advice. Your surgeon will provide a personalised return-to-activity plan.

Long-term monitoring

Breast implants are not lifetime devices. Additional operations may be needed, and complications can occur, so long-term monitoring is an important part of the decision.

Revision surgery

Some patients require revision surgery at some point. Understanding this possibility in advance is part of realistic planning.
